summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% to INR 6,776 mn and EBITDA to INR 600 mn, mainly from an INR 10 mn order deferred to H2.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 6,776 mn versus INR 7,080 mn a year earlier, a 4% decline, which management attributed mainly to an order pushed from Q1 into the latter half of FY27. EBITDA fell to INR 600 mn from INR 1,406 mn, and the company posted a loss before tax of about INR 512 mn after finance costs of about INR 370 mn and an FX loss of about INR 117.3 mn. The CDMO segment revenue fell to INR 5,343 mn while Marketable Molecules rose to INR 1,432 mn. Management guided to single-digit group revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin similar to or slightly above FY26, and said a promoter-level ECB of up to CHF 200 mn is expected to close in 60-90 days.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 5,343 mn, down from INR 6,112 mn; EBITDA margin 6.3% vs 17.9%, hit by deferred order and FX loss.

segments.name: Marketable Molecules (cholesterol, Vitamin D and analogues)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,432 mn, up from INR 968 mn; margin normalised as cholesterol sales outweighed analogues versus a high analogue quarter last year. Vitamin D and analogues sales and margin reportedly rose.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue growth guided to single digits; France and Swiss CDMO growth slower than planned.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected similar to FY26, possibly slightly higher.
Indian entity revenue guided to grow 25-35% in FY27 with operating margin near 10% (analyst's characterisation, not explicitly confirmed by management).
FY28-29: at least double-digit growth in France and India; group revenue growth above 10% YoY; EBITDA margin closer to 25-26% seen before EDQM issues.
No quarterly guidance; management said Q2 is difficult to guide. Net debt expected CHF 140-150 mn (excluding promoter infusion), reducing by about CHF 8-9 mn.
Interest expense guided at about INR 130-140 crores for the full year (about INR 35-40 crores per quarter).
Promoter ECB up to CHF 200 mn at 4% all-inclusive, 10-year tenor, to prepay high-cost India debt; expected in 60-90 days. RBI approval reportedly received.
capex_capacity: Two tech transfers from Carbogen Amcis Switzerland to India: one commercial contract signed with a US company (Switzerland to Bavla, to complete within FY27); a second legacy project approved by a Swiss MNC and already initiated; three more in advanced discussion.
Second co-investment with the Japanese ADC customer is in progress, with operations expected in calendar 2027.
Naroda and Bavla hold certifications from all major international health authorities; Naroda passed a Korea MFDS inspection and is under US FDA observation; two CEPs granted by EDQM.
Restarting some API production at the Netherlands entity.
Inspections scheduled for later in 2026 at Carbogen Amcis sites (no details given).
demand_pricing: New commercial leadership: Angela Ameriks joined as Global CCO; new India sales leadership; hiring in UK, Central Europe and US West Coast (start 1 Sept).
SPRINT early-phase acquisition initiative reported as successful; over 13 late-phase projects in drug substance portfolio, including PPQ campaigns.
Drug product (Saint-Beauzire, France): RFP volumes up and quotation rates raised, though market is challenging; big pharma audits had positive outcomes.
Naroda: CDMO RFPs rising steeply, several in final negotiation; semiconductor and fine-chemical projects in progress.
Biotech funding slowdown is weighing on development revenue; destocking by customers after pandemic stockpiling noted.
ADC-related revenue in the quarter was about INR 150 crores, including linker, payload and hyper molecule.
Specialty business: new wool grease sources at better prices; new markets in Vietnam, Africa and South America.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 revenue and EBITDA margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-digit revenue growth for FY27; EBITDA margin similar to last year, maybe slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: How will the high-cost debt be refinanced?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter entity to raise up to CHF 200 mn in foreign currency and infuse it as ECB into the Indian entity, at 4% all-inclusive for 10 years; expected in 60-90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why does cash stay overseas rather than repay India debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary-to-parent loans are not permitted, and repatriation via dividends triggers tax leakage, so Swiss cash is kept as deposits to fund overseas needs.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 net debt and interest expense?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about CHF 140-150 mn, falling CHF 8-9 mn; interest expense about INR 130-140 crores for the full year, excluding promoter infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 550 crore EBITDA for the remaining three quarters achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not be INR 200 mn each quarter, but expects EBITDA similar to last year, with focus on the top line.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company swung between profit and loss quarter to quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lumpy B2B shipments tied to new chemical entities, a largely fixed cost base (employee cost about 50% of P&L), and Q4 typically the strongest quarter; each INR 10 mn revenue could add about 70% to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much goodwill remains and is it amortised?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated goodwill is above INR 4,000 crores, restated at closing rates and not amortised; standalone goodwill is about INR 550 crores and is amortised; original INR 1,350 crores.

financial_highlights.value: INR 18.6 mn absolute (per call); margin normalised

risks_watch: Promoter-level ECB of up to CHF 200 mn (4% all-inclusive, 10-year) expected in 60-90 days; watch for actual fund flow into the Indian entity and prepayment of high-cost India debt and NCDs.
Q2 FY27 is hard to guide; full-year single-digit revenue growth requires a sharp H2 ramp, and management said Q1 EBITDA of INR 600 mn will not be repeated at INR 200 mn per quarter.
French drug product entity (Saint-Beauzire) taking longer than expected to reach breakeven; CDMO revenue from RFPs may only convert into revenue in FY28.
Swiss CDMO exposed to slower biotech funding and customer destocking; FX (USD/CHF) swings continue to hit other expenses (INR 117.3 mn loss in Q1).
Goodwill of over INR 4,000 crore on consolidation is not amortised and relies on annual impairment testing; standalone goodwill of about INR 550 crore continues to be amortised.
Quarterly earnings lumpiness tied to new chemical entity shipments; ADC co-investment capacity with the Japanese customer expected in calendar 2027.
key_quotes: We do expect single-digit growth as far as the revenues are concerned.
Well, it won't be 200 for each of the quarters, but we'll have to see again depending upon how the shipments go out, etc.
The important thing is to focus on the top line.
Well, from a net debt perspective, I think we should be somewhere around CHF 140-150 million and this is in Swiss franc, and that would be the right way to look at our debt.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on medium-term growth and the promoter ECB, but cautious and non-committal on near-term numbers: it declined to guide Q2 and said the full-group revenue growth would be single digit for FY27 because French and Swiss CDMO ramp-ups are slower than planned. Pushback on quarterly losses and debt was answered with mechanics and timelines rather than hard figures.

adds.what: Tech transfer from Carbogen Amcis Switzerland to Bavla, India (one commercial contract signed with US company, to complete within FY27)
Second co-investment with Japanese ADC customer, operations expected calendar 2027
Restart of some API production at Netherlands entity

growth.why: Management guides FY27 group revenue to single-digit growth (a cut), with EBITDA margin similar to FY26 and FY28-29 revenue growth above 10%, backed by two tech transfers to Bavla, a Japanese ADC co-investment due CY2027, and a commercial team build-out, but no specific capacity or order numbers were given for the single-digit FY27 target.
